transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-21 16:00 PST | Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Gomez (Redwood SE), Lina Zhang (CSM) — Velori: Ari Novak (Head of AI), Priya Shah (Platform Eng), Jon Bell (Finance)

Summary:
This was a QBR-style health/checkin focused on adoption velocity, cost drivers from recent spike, and options for moving from hosted to a Dedicated commitment vs hybrid VPC. Covered reliability incidents in last 30 days (2 brief timeouts), possible quantization and batching savings, and an ask to run concrete benchmarks and share pricing models. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics discussed:
- Usage trend and anomalous burst on Feb 9 causing 17% cost bump
- Latency SLOs vs batching tradeoffs for batch-sensitive customers
- Dedicated capacity vs hosted: commit tiers and burst behavior
- Private/VPC and KMS requirements for regulated workloads
- Recent incidents and root-cause (cache eviction + routing failover)
- Pilot scope and benchmarks required before commit

Action items (also in metadata): see list above

Transcript body (timestamps are approximate; transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Maya: alright, everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run through usage, what happened with that cost blip, and talk through options for Dedicated and a pilot.
[00:14] Ari: yep thanks, Maya. Quick note — we're calling in from London so slight delay. But yeah we saw a spike around Feb 9 where token spend jumped about 17%, we think it's related to a new feature rollout.
[00:28] Priya: yeah it coincided with the A/B for the new summarization path. We had more long-context requests and some chained calls.
[00:40] Carlos: ok, that aligns. When you say chained calls, do you mean sequential multi-turn prompting where the client re-queries with the KV persisted? Or were you re-creating sessions?
[00:54] Priya: hm, probably re-creating sessions. The front end does a fresh session on each click sometimes. We need to confirm.
[01:05] Jon: from finance — that spike translated to a material overrun in February. We need to understand unit economics if we move to Dedicated.
[01:15] Maya: understood. So quick framing — Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit, but you trade some flexibility. There's burst policies to handle spikes but we need to size it.
[01:28] Ari: can you remind us of the burst mechanics? Last time the doc i saw said "burst lanes" but it wasn't clear.
[01:36] Carlos: yeah for Dedicated you get provisioned pools, and you can configure autoscale with burst allowance — essentially short-term extra capacity for traffic spikes. The behavior is: sustained usage beyond capacity will queue or route to hosted fallback depending on policy. Some of our customers set automatic fallback to a cheaper, compatible model to preserve latency.
[01:57] Priya: fallback to a cheaper model — previous note said output quality dropped. That's a concern for product.
[02:07] Carlos: right, which is why we recommend a canary plan: pilot with a small commit, enable canary route rules, and verify output with your eval set. Also quantization tradeoffs can save cost while keeping quality.
[02:23] Ari: about quantization — we did see a 1-2% difference in ROUGE on internal tests. How much cost saving realistically?
[02:32] Maya: ballpark, 20-40% depending on model and prompt length. But it's workload dependent. We'll put a profile in the pricing workbook.
[02:40] Priya: can you also run a KV cache warm vs cold test? We suspect the Feb 9 incident had a few cache evictions that caused token duplication.
[02:50] Carlos: absolutely. We'll run a 24-hour run with your representative prompt mix. Please send the top-100 prompt templates and the traffic shape (p95, p99) — that will make the benchmark realistic.
[03:03] Priya: noted, will send by tomorrow.
[03:08] Jon: also, security — SOC2 in place? Our legal will ask about audit logs and KMS.
[03:16] Lina: yes — Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, we have KMS integrations and audit logs. For Private/VPC deployments we can enable customer-managed KMS and longer retention for logs. I'll attach the security pack.
[03:30] Ari: good. We have a compliance window in late March where infra needs to validate KMS & SSO.
[03:36] Maya: ok let's aim pilot kickoff before that.
[03:40] 
[05:02] (long section discussing cost model)
[05:02] Maya: so the model we usually use is per-token hosted pricing, and for Dedicated we show effective per-token cost after commit amortization. For example, a 3-month mid-tier commit reduces per-token by ~28% for this workload shape. But we need exact traffic to compute.
[06:15] Jon: if we commit, do we lose credits for unused capacity? Finance is worried about overprovision.
[06:25] Carlos: there's a burn model — reserved commit is billed but you get the pool. Unused capacity can be shifted to other regions or workloads within the org depending on contract. We can also structure a laddered commit to reduce risk.
[06:40] Priya: laddered commit sounds interesting — can you send examples?
[06:45] Maya: yes, I'll put examples in the workbook.
[07:01] Ari: about the reliability incident — can you walk us through what Redwood found?
[07:08] Carlos: from our side we saw two short outages: one was an internal routing flap between AZs that caused requests to hit a fallback path; another was a cache eviction cascade when a maintenance job started and kicked KV caches. The second is the likeliest cause of duplicated tokens and extra cost.
[07:33] Priya: wow maintenance job — was that scheduled?
[07:36] Carlos: it was a background compaction that misaligned with peak in one region. We've added better maintenance windows and KV warmup to prevent full evictions.
[07:48] Ari: did you correlate request IDs so we can map our logs?
[07:51] Carlos: yes we keep trace IDs. We'll share the incident playbook link and the trace log sample (redacted).
[08:00] Maya: Link to incident notes: https://redwood.app/notes/velori-incident-20270209 (placeholder)
[08:06] 
[09:20] (discussion about pilot scope)
[09:20] Maya: recommended pilot scope: 2-week bench with representative traffic, run Dedicated small commit or hosted with tuned batching/quantization, measure p50/p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, and quality regressions.
[09:35] Priya: we'll want to test both VPC private deployment and hosted fallback. Can you support VPC peering?
[09:44] Carlos: yes we support VPC peering and our Private deployment has customer-managed KMS. For early pilots we often run a hybrid where control plane sits with Redwood but inference lives in customer VPC.
[09:58] Ari: any changes needed on our side? network ACLs, endpoints?
[10:03] Carlos: standard egress rules and a small NAT range. We'll share a checklist.
[10:09] Maya: Checklist link (shared): https://redwood.app/velori/pilot-checklist
[10:14] 
[12:00] (pricing specifics and worksheets)
[12:00] Maya: Jon, finance — we'll send a worked example of 3 commit scenarios (small, mid, large) with effective per-token math. That'll include burst allowances and laddering.
[12:12] Jon: please include a scenario where we can transfer unused capacity across business units — that's important for our procurement team.
[12:20] Maya: noted.
[14:05] (questions about routing policies and fallbacks)
[14:05] Priya: curious about automatic fallback to hosted — do you throttle first or route?
[14:12] Carlos: routing policy priority: primary pool -> autoscale -> fallback model in hosted. You can set SLOs per route so the system prefers lower-latency paths when available.
[14:27] Priya: ok. We need a route that doesn't change model behavior much — so same family/model but smaller context length maybe?
[14:36] Carlos: yep that's the approach; it's called model-variant fallback. We'll help pick variants.
[16:00] (misc clarifications)
[16:00] Ari: timeline check — we'd like to decide by end of March for Q2 ramp. Is that feasible?
[16:07] Maya: yes if we do pilot early March and get benchmarks by March 10, you can decide in time.
[16:15] Lina: I'll coordinate the pilot calendar and sync invites.
[16:20] Priya: one more, encryption at rest — does your Private option allow HSM integration?
[16:27] Carlos: yes customer HSM/KMS can be integrated; we'll add the HSM integration checklist.
[16:33] 
[18:00] (wrap-up and recap)
[18:00] Maya: quick recap: Priya to send traffic shape + top prompts by 2027-02-24; Maya to send pricing workbook with commit scenarios by 2027-02-25; Carlos to run KV warm/cold benchmark and 24-hr latency run and share by 2027-03-01; Jon to confirm budget window by 2027-02-28; Lina to schedule pilot week of 2027-03-07.
[18:30] Ari: sounds good. Please include links to the security pack and the checklist in the follow-up email.
[18:36] Maya: will do.
[18:40] Jon: ok thanks, that was helpful.
[18:44] (small crosstalk, people leaving)
